title: Phone Plan
primary_metric: total monthly cost (with tax) at the family's current 2-line need
new_coverage_note: Legacy-conversion case (see legacy_conversion_note). Both are real, freshly-forced new coverage (n=0 pre-conversion): D3 explicitly requires finding the break-even line count by solving the two carriers' cost equations as a system of linear equations -- not a skill any deliverable in this case could be completed without.
legacy_conversion_note: Original 2021 case's Appendix A/B referenced carrier pricing/coverage-map images that were not captured as machine-readable text (screenshots or dead links, not extracted by python-docx) -- the real 2020-era Verizon/T-Mobile numbers are not recoverable from the source .docx, and 2026 pricing for either real carrier would require fresh external research this conversion did not do. Kept the real story (the Handleson family, Nate's work travel and hotspot need, Fiona's coverage concern, the family's stated plan to add a 3rd and 4th line within a year or two) but designed clean, self-contained, given pricing for fictional 'Carrier V' and 'Carrier T' -- same convention as Cold Chain's real WHO specs under a fictional district. The linear cost structure (flat rate for 2 lines, fixed additional-line rate) is a genuine simplification of how real carriers price multi-line plans, not an arbitrary invention.

modeling_assumptions.text: Idaho's state plan tax is a flat 8%, applied to the pre-tax total in Appendix A's pricing.

Both carriers' additional-line rate (Appendix A) is assumed to hold when the 3rd/4th line is actually added -- not a guarantee either carrier publishes, but the only reasonable basis to budget from today.

deliverables.text: A linear cost equation for each carrier (cost = rate*lines + fixed), with slope and y-intercept identified.
Total monthly cost, with tax, for both carriers at 2, 3, and 4 lines.
The break-even line count, found by solving the two carriers' equations as a system of equations.
A recommendation on which carrier costs less at 2 lines, and whether that holds after adding a 3rd line.

balance.argument_a: Carrier V's per-line rate beyond 2 lines ($15) is far cheaper than Carrier T's ($25) -- the two carriers' cost lines cross at exactly 3 lines ($102.60 with tax, both), and the Handleson family's own stated plan is to add Charity's line, their 3rd, within the next year. Choosing on today's 2-line price alone optimizes for a need that expires in roughly twelve months.
balance.argument_b: At the family's actual, current 2-line need, Carrier T costs $75.60 a month with tax against Carrier V's $86.40 -- a real 14.29% difference, and T includes unlimited hotspot data against V's capped 15 GB, which matters directly for Nate's stated hotspot use while traveling. A 3rd line is a plan, not a signed contract; the family is paying today's bill with today's money.
balance.margin_basis: Total monthly cost with tax at the family's current 2-line need (Appendix A/B). D3's break-even analysis (exactly 3 lines) is real, disclosed context behind argument_a without being the graded primary metric -- see derived{} for the full worked equations.

derived._note: Computed during conversion from Appendix A/B's given pricing; case-readiness should re-derive independently, not just trust this block.

cohort_bands.note: Anchors 2-3 run as written; the room debates today's price vs. the 1-year plan before the break-even math settles part of it.
Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; D1's two equations are derived together instead of one-at-a-time.
No vote to take -- Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position instead of a cold-call; guide plays devil's advocate directly.
